```
[Issue #7063]  Fix CommonGrants OpenAPI docs (#8767)

## Summary

Fixes #7063 Common grants open-api endpoint not working

## Changes proposed

The open-api endpoint for common-grants search were not working due to
missing example values in the marshmallow schema. This caused the search
request to populate the various keys with the value types e.g. "string"
instead of an actual example string.

## Context for reviewers

<!-- Technical or background context, more in-depth details of the
implementation, and anything else you'd like reviewers to know about
that will help them understand the changes in the PR. -->

The only changes in this PR that are under our control are the changes
to the python file. The workflow to make changes to the yaml is to
update the Python file, then run `make openapi-spec-common-grants` to
generate the updated yaml file that is included in this PR.

## Validation steps

<!-- Manual testing instructions, as well as any helpful references
(screenshots, GIF demos, code examples or output). -->
1. Checkout branch
2. Run the following commands to start the API `# Start API with data
make init 
make db-seed-local && make populate-search-opportunities
make run-logs
```
3. Go to `http://localhost:8080/docs` in your browswer
4. Scroll down to `Common Grants Protocol`
5. Open the POST `search` request and select `try it out`
6. Note that the request body now populates with the correct values and when clicking `Execute` the server returns a response.

---------

infra(nofos): migrate to template-infra management (#8548)

## Summary

- Brings nofos infrastructure under template-infra management via
`nava-platform infra add-app`
- Creates `.template-infra/app-nofos.yml` tracking file so nofos
receives future template upgrades
- Restores all nofos-specific customizations (secrets, domains, database
config, owner tags, provider versions) on top of the template skeleton
- Adds new CI/CD workflow files from the template
(pr-environment-checks, pr-environment-destroy, vulnerability-scans)
- Adds identity_provider.tf scaffolding (disabled) and monitoring module
from template

Relates to navapbc/tss-internal#3

### Key nofos customizations preserved:
- `owner = "bloomworks"` tags (not "navapbc")
- `readonly_root_filesystem = false` (Django needs writable fs)
- 6 manual secrets: API_TOKEN, DJANGO_ALLOWED_HOSTS, DOCRAPTOR_API_KEY,
GRABZIT_APPLICATION_KEY, GRABZIT_APPLICATION_SECRET, SECRET_KEY
- `has_external_non_aws_service = true` (DocRaptor, GrabzIt)
- `enable_notifications = true`
- Domain names: nofos.dev.simpler.grants.gov, nofos.simpler.grants.gov,
nofos.training.simpler.grants.gov
- Database engine_version passthrough (training uses 17.5)
- Terraform 1.14.3, AWS provider ~>6.13.0 (database), >=5.81.0 (service)

### template-infra improvement suggestions:
- **`infra adopt-app` command** — merge-aware alternative to `add-app`
for existing apps that preserves customizations
- **Configurable `owner` tag** — template hardcodes "navapbc", should be
a variable
- **`database_engine_version` support** — needed by nofos, not currently
a template feature
- **Preserve `.s3.tfbackend` on add-app** — detect and skip overwriting
live state pointers
- **Secret module migration guide** — document `modules/secret` ->
`modules/secrets` refactor path

## Test plan

- [x] `terraform validate` passes in app-config
- [x] `terraform validate` passes in build-repository
- [x] `terraform validate` passes in database
- [x] `terraform validate` passes in service
- [x] `nava-platform infra info .` lists nofos as a managed app
- [x] `terraform plan -var="environment_name=dev"` for service layer
shows no destructive changes
- [x] `terraform plan -var="environment_name=dev"` for database layer
shows no destructive changes

[Issue #8105] Add AuthZ to workflow event API (#8775)

## Summary
Fixes / Work for #8105

## Changes proposed
* Adds AuthZ to workflow event API
* Sets up a user locally we can use to send events

## Context for reviewers
This enforces authentication for the event API. There are two ways to be
authenticated:
* We have an internal user privilege that lets you send events and we
won't check - this is mostly for testing and demoing.
* Having privileges for doing the approval event against the agency that
owns the entity associated with the workflow

Importantly, starting a workflow is not an approval event, except for
our internal user, you actually can't start a workflow via this API (and
that's just allowed for testing purposes). All start workflow events
will be done by other endpoints, for example to start the publish
opportunity workflow, publish an opportunity and that endpoint will do
it.

## Validation steps

Found an opportunity locally (doesn't matter which) and grabbed their
ID. Authenticated with the User API Key Auth with the new user using the
`internal_workflow_user_key` key. Can then call the event API like so.

```json
{
  "event_type": "start_workflow",
  "start_workflow_context": {
    "entity_id": "e43617f3-19e9-4ab2-a1ca-e6a57326090d",
    "entity_type": "opportunity",
    "workflow_type": "initial_prototype"
  }
}
```

If you try with any other user, you'll get rejected. More granular
testing is done in the unit tests.
